name: Marienplatz
description: Munich’s main square, in front of the neo-Gothic New Town Hall, whose tower has a mechanical Glockenspiel that plays most days at 11am.

name: Ludwig Maximilian University
description: The university’s main building, where White Rose students were arrested in 1943 for spreading anti-Nazi leaflets. A memorial is inside.

name: Alte Pinakothek
description: One of the oldest public galleries in the world, opened in 1836, with European paintings from the Middle Ages to the 18th century.

name: Residenz
description: The city palace of Bavaria’s rulers: courtyards, state rooms, a treasury and a small rococo court theatre.

name: Olympic Stadium
description: The stadium built for the 1972 Olympics, under a tent-like roof of acrylic panels, in a park laid out on wartime rubble.

name: Connollystraße 31
description: The building in the Olympic Village where Israeli athletes were taken hostage during the 1972 Olympics. A plaque marks it.

name: Nymphenburg Palace
description: The baroque summer palace of Bavaria’s rulers, with large gardens and the Gallery of Beauties, a room of portraits of women.

name: Odeonsplatz
description: A grand square at the south end of Ludwigstraße, with the Feldherrnhalle loggia and the yellow Theatine Church.

name: Hofbräuhaus
description: A huge beer hall that began as the royal brewery in 1589, with long shared tables, a brass band and its own beer.

name: Isartor
description: One of three surviving gates of the medieval city wall, on the east side of the old town.

name: Glyptothek
description: A museum of ancient Greek and Roman sculpture in a temple-like building on Königsplatz, opened in 1830.

name: Führerbau
places: Führerbau, now the University of Music and Performing Arts
description: A Nazi party building on Königsplatz where the 1938 Munich Agreement was signed. It is now a university of music.

name: National Theatre (Bavarian State Opera)
description: The neoclassical opera house on Max-Joseph-Platz, home of the Bavarian State Opera and Ballet, rebuilt after wartime bombing.

name: Bavarian State Library
description: One of Europe’s largest research libraries, in a long 19th-century building on Ludwigstraße.

name: Musicland Studios
description: A former recording studio in the basement of the Arabella high-rise, where many rock and disco records were made in the 1970s and 80s.

name: Kurt Eisner memorial
description: A memorial set into the pavement where Kurt Eisner, Bavaria’s first republican prime minister, was shot dead in 1919.

name: Hofgarten arcades
places: Hofgarten arcades, site of the 1937 Degenerate Art show
description: The arcades around the old court garden beside the Residenz, where the Nazis’ 1937 ‘Degenerate Art’ exhibition was held.

name: Allianz Arena
description: FC Bayern’s stadium on the northern edge of the city, wrapped in panels that light up at night, with the club museum inside.
